sections.html:
Voters approved incorporation on November 3, 2015, and Millcreek became a city on December 28, 2016. A 2012 attempt had failed with about 40 percent support. For years before that the area was a county township, created by Salt Lake County in 2002 to give residents a stronger voice in planning and to keep neighboring cities from annexing it.

The first mayor and council took office in 2016. City hall is therefore young, and some rules, ADU policy included, are still being refined. Ask the city for the current version before you rely on any summary, this page included.

The city is mostly residential and fairly settled. Settlement dates to 1848, the area stayed rural until after World War II, and suburban building then pushed south from Salt Lake City until most of it was built out by the 1980s. Expect a lot of postwar through 1980s houses, where a buyer's inspector looks first at the roof, plumbing and wiring.

The median value is a citywide figure. It does not predict what a specific house will bring, particularly a hillside lot or one with an extra unit.

sections.h2: Where Millcreek sits and its four community councils
sections.html:
Millcreek lies south of Salt Lake City and South Salt Lake and north of Murray and Holladay, with Mill Creek Canyon rising directly to the east. Four community councils divide it.

  • Canyon Rim, in the northeast, has steeper ground.
  • East Mill Creek sits near the mouth of the canyon.
  • Mount Olympus takes in Olympus Cove in the eastern foothills.
  • The Millcreek area covers the western and central parts, which are the most densely developed.

Five ZIP codes cover the city: 84106, 84107, 84109, 84117 and 84124. Because a mailing address alone can't tell you whether a house is inside Millcreek, look up the parcel record.

Millcreek has a sensitive lands ordinance covering faults, liquefaction areas, steep slopes and the Mill Creek floodplain, along with avalanche and rockfall zones, alluvial fans, stream corridors, ridgelines and the wildland and urban interface. Mount Olympus debris flow areas roughly track slopes steeper than 30 percent.

Depending on the hazard, a project may need a fault survey, a soils study or a slope analysis and buildable area test. Canyon Rim lots are the usual example of steep ground.

  • These rules bite when someone builds or adds on, so they matter most if your buyer wants an addition.
  • Check with the city before relying on any relief option for single-family homes.
  • An owner who disputes a hazard on a lot can submit a site-specific geologic report to the county geologist.

The canyon is undeveloped national forest land in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest, just east of the East Mill Creek and Mount Olympus neighborhoods. It charges a $5 per vehicle fee on the way out, sells a $50 annual pass, and closes its upper half to vehicles from November 1 through July 1. Dogs may run off leash on odd-numbered days only.

If your house is near the canyon road, expect buyers to ask about weekend traffic and trail parking. A straight answer helps more than a glossy one.

Millcreek permits an accessory dwelling unit only on a lot with an owner-occupied home. The city records a notice on the title saying so, which means a buyer's title company will see it.

  • Internal and attached units can be short-term rentals with an ADU application and a Millcreek business license. Detached units cannot.
  • Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed in every ADU type, with an ADU compliance letter and a business license.
  • Each unit needs at least one off-street parking stall, and a separate utility meter is not allowed.
  • A detached unit needs an R-1 or A zone, a lot of at least 8,000 square feet, up to 1,000 square feet of floor area and a rear-yard location.

Since the rules turn on owner occupancy, an investor who buys the house can't assume the unit stays rentable. If you built a basement apartment without a permit, say so early.

Utah taxes a primary residence on 55 percent of market value, while a second home is taxed on all of it. To qualify, a household must use the home as its primary domicile for 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and it can claim only one. The exemption does not follow a sale automatically, so a buyer who moves in files a new application with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. A late filing can cost the owner the exemption for that tax year.

A landlord renting to a full-time tenant can also claim it with a declaration signed by every owner. Starting January 1, 2027, a 2026 change requires owners to file Form TC-473A whenever ownership changes, including deed or trust transfers.

Tax notices come from Salt Lake County by November 1. The bill can be paid without penalty through November 30, and anything outstanding is delinquent on December 1. A fall sale needs a quick conversation with the title company about how the current bill is divided at closing.

sections.h2: Preparing a Millcreek house for sale
sections.html:
Millcreek houses vary a lot, from flat western neighborhoods to foothill lots on Canyon Rim and Olympus Cove, so gather the facts that apply to yours. For a hillside lot, find any geologic or slope reports. For a house with an extra unit, find the ADU compliance letter and business license, or be ready to explain why there isn't one. For an older house, jot down the age of the roof, plumbing and wiring.

None of this has to be perfect before you reach out. A cash buyer works from the house as it is, and honest notes about its problems speed up the offer.

sections.h2: Selling a Millcreek house for cash
sections.html:
Selling to us for cash means no mortgage underwriting, no appraisal gap and no staging. We price the house on its condition, and a title company runs the signing and files the deed with the county.

  1. Send the address and an honest description.
  2. We go over the details and name a price.
  3. Agree to it, and the title company drafts the closing paperwork.
  4. The deed is recorded and you are paid at closing.

This route tends to suit owners with an unpermitted unit, a hillside lot with a long repair list, or a stalled probate. Have your deed, any ADU letter or notice on the title, and the latest tax notice handy so the conversation goes quickly.

faqs.q: When did Millcreek become a city?
faqs.a: The vote was November 3, 2015, and the city incorporated December 28, 2016. Before that it was a county township, from 2002.

faqs.q: Can I rent out an accessory dwelling unit in Millcreek?
faqs.a: Yes, provided an owner lives in the main home and the unit has a compliance letter. Short-term renting works for internal and attached units with an application and business license. Detached ones can't be short-term rentals.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Millcreek?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $627,200, a citywide number that can't price your own house.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Millcreek?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty on the current year's bill. After that, the balance turns delinquent on December 1.

faqs.q: Does the primary residence exemption transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: No, the buyer has to apply again. The deadline is September 15, and filing late can forfeit that tax year's exemption.
